classification.difficultyReason: Compare road connections with four network representations, distinguishing an additional connection and parallel edges.

content.prompt: Which network diagram represents the roads and junctions shown on this map?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6 road map at lower left
spec.description: Five marked points and curved roads. The road descending from K meets the P–M road at an unmarked junction; no vertex marker is added there.
spec.mathematics: Outer roads KL, KM, MN and NL; interior roads LP, PN and PM, with a road from K terminating at an unmarked point on PM.
spec.answerVisibility: All roads and five labelled points are permanent givens.

spec.description: Straight-edged network with option label A.
spec.mathematics: Edges KL, KM, LN, MN, LP, PM and PN.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent answer choice; no correctness indication.

spec.description: Option A's edges plus a curved KP edge.
spec.mathematics: Edges KL, KM, LN, MN, LP, PM, PN and KP.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent answer choice; no correctness indication.

spec.description: Option A's edges plus a second, curved KM edge.
spec.mathematics: Edges KL, LN, MN, LP, PM, PN and two distinct KM edges.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent answer choice; no correctness indication.

spec.description: Corrected option D: explicit unlabelled junction between P and M; K joins that junction.
spec.mathematics: Six vertices, nine edges. Outer KL, KM, MN, NL; LP, PN, P–junction, junction–M and K–junction.

answer.worked: The road from K meets the P–M road at an additional junction. D includes this junction and preserves all nine road sections, including LP and PN and the outer roads. Correct answer: D.
